extra.message: The '/ping' route builds a shell command with 'ping ' + req.query['id'] and passes it directly to child_process.exec() with no sanitization or allowlisting. An attacker can supply id like '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd' or use shell metacharacters (&&, |, `` ` ``, $()) to execute arbitrary OS commands.

The '/eval' route concatenates the raw query parameters 'id' and 'id2' and passes them directly to JavaScript's eval(). This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary server-side JavaScript (e.g. id=require('child_process').exec('id')//), leading to full remote code execution.

The '/api/users' login handler detects if req.body.password contains '{' and, if so, JSON.parse()s it and uses the resulting object directly as the password field in a MongoDB find() query. An attacker can submit a password like {"$ne":""} (or {"$gt":""}) to inject MongoDB query operators, bypassing password verification and authenticating without knowing a valid password. The 'email' field is likewise taken unvalidated from JSON body and can also carry operators.

The '/getdata' route JSON.parse()s the raw 'id' query parameter and uses the resulting value directly as the 'id' field in a MongoDB find() query. Because JSON.parse can produce an object, an attacker can pass id={"$ne":null} (or any Mongo operator) to alter query logic and dump arbitrary user records instead of the intended single record.

The '/a6_misconfig' route JSON.parse()s the raw 'accountno' field from the request body and passes the result unvalidated into a MongoDB find({accountno: accno}) query. An attacker-supplied object (e.g. {"$gt":""}) is interpreted as a Mongo query operator, allowing the account-number filter to be bypassed and unrelated records disclosed.

The '/insecure_deserialization' route builds an object embedding the unsanitized, user-controlled 'userid' body field, serializes it with node-serialize (which encodes function properties as executable '_$$ND_FUNC$$_' strings), and immediately calls serialize.unserialize() on the result, invoking the embedded function. node-serialize's unserialize() is known (CVE-2017-5941) to execute arbitrary JavaScript when the serialized string contains a crafted '_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){...}()' payload; because the 'name' value is attacker-controlled and only the 'say' function is trusted here, any input that can break out of the serialized string context (e.g. via unescaped characters) can achieve remote code execution.

The '/a3sensitive' route takes an arbitrary 'id' query parameter and returns the matching user record from the 'users' collection with no session/authentication check and no verification that the requester owns that record. Any caller can enumerate ids (1, 2, 3, ...) to dump other users' data (name, age, etc.), a classic Insecure Direct Object Reference.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The '/insecure_dor' route looks up records in the 'a5_insecure_dor' collection by an attacker-supplied 'accountno' from the request body with no authentication middleware and no check that the requester is authorized to view that account. Any client can enumerate account numbers to retrieve other users' account records.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The controller takes response['data'].search — which is the raw, attacker-controlled 'id' query parameter echoed back verbatim by the server's '/xss_r' route (xvna/index.js:162-176, res.json({search: id})) — and passes it to $sce.trustAsHtml(), explicitly bypassing Angular's built-in ngSanitize protection (the app has 'ngSanitize' loaded in app.js). The resulting trustedMessage is presumably rendered with ng-bind-html, so a payload like ?id= executes in the victim's browser.

The '/a3sensitive_header' route serializes and returns the full raw req.headers object to the client with no authentication check and no filtering, potentially exposing internal/proxy-added headers (e.g. cookies, authorization tokens, internal routing headers) that should not be disclosed back to arbitrary callers.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The express-session middleware is configured with a hardcoded, literal secret string ("Your secret key"). Anyone with source access can forge valid session cookies, and since the same fixed secret is used across all deployments of this codebase, session integrity cannot be trusted.

A hardcoded credential-like string ("impraveensingh") is assigned to an undeclared global variable 'secret' inside the '/eval' handler. Hardcoding secret material directly in source is a credential-management weakness even though this particular value is unused elsewhere.

The '/a6_misconfig' route sends the raw MongoDB driver error object directly to the client via res.json(err) on both the connection error and query error paths, potentially leaking internal implementation details (driver stack traces, connection info) to an attacker.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The express-session middleware is initialized with only a 'secret' option — no 'cookie: { secure: true, httpOnly: true }', no 'resave'/'saveUninitialized' flags are set. Without an explicit secure cookie flag, the session cookie can be transmitted over plaintext HTTP, exposing it to network interception.
